area: c2c role-designer "wizard" — agent role-file authoring surfaces (c2c agent new / refine, role-designer persona)
summary: The "wizard tui" the operator remembers is two distinct things, NEITHER of which is a real TUI. (1) The closest thing to a wizard is `c2c agent new` run with no flags on an interactive TTY: a sequential numbered-menu prompt loop (description → role type → compatible clients → theme → snippets → auto-join rooms → open-in-editor) built on hand-rolled `prompt_nonempty`/`prompt_choice`/`prompt_multi_select` readline helpers — no curses/ANSI, no cursor nav, no back-button, no validation beyond range checks. It writes a `.c2c/roles/<NAME>.md` template skeleton, then suggests `c2c agent refine`. (2) The actual "role-designer" is an LLM PERSONA, not a UI: `.c2c/roles/role-designer.md` is a system-prompt that instructs a coding agent to interview a human and author a role file. `c2c agent refine <name>` reads the on-disk draft, builds a kickoff prompt embedding it, and launches a full coding-CLI session (Claude/OpenCode/Codex/Kimi) in a tmux pane (`--mode Pane`) running the role-designer persona. The interaction is a free-form chat in that spawned agent's pane — the operator talks to an LLM, the LLM edits the file in place with its Edit tool, then calls stop_self. There is no structured terminal interface at any point. A third fragment, `c2c start <client>` for an unknown alias, has an inline one-line `input_line` prompt asking for a role class (c2c.ml:9070). NOTABLE: `role_designer_embedded.content` (the entire role_designer_embedded.ml module) is compiled-in DEAD CODE — it is in the dune modules list but has zero runtime consumers; the active path reads the on-disk `.c2c/roles/role-designer.md` and errors if absent rather than falling back to the embedded copy.

c2c_agent.ml:13-50 — hand-rolled readline primitives `prompt_nonempty`, `prompt_choice`, `prompt_multi_select`; recursion-on-invalid-input, no ANSI/curses, no arrow-key nav, no escape-to-cancel

c2c_agent.ml:664-750 `agent_refine_term` (`c2c agent refine <name>`) — reads `.c2c/roles/<name>.md`, builds an interview/refine kickoff prompt, calls `run_ephemeral_agent ~role:"role-designer" ~mode:Pane`; the role-designer 'wizard' is this spawned LLM session, not a UI. Has `--agent-mode` (DM caller for clarification + stop_self) vs default (interview in pane)

c2c_agent.ml:402-406 — run_ephemeral_agent hard-errors `role file not found` if .c2c/roles/role-designer.md is absent; it does NOT use the embedded copy as a fallback

ocaml/cli/dune:3 — role_designer_embedded listed in (modules ...) so it compiles, but grep across ocaml/ for `Role_designer_embedded.`/`role_designer_embedded` outside its own file + the codegen recipe returns no matches (dead value)
c2c_agent.ml:829-839 `agent_group` + 1013-1016 `roles_group`; wired at c2c.ml:12321. Commands: agent new|list|delete|rename|refine|run; roles compile|validate
c2c.ml:323 / c2c.ml:9070-9099 — `c2c start` inline single-line role prompt for unknown aliases (uses Role_templates.render for known role classes)
ocaml/test/test_agent_refine.ml — only exercises `c2c agent refine ... --dry-run` (string-matches kickoff prompt); no test drives the actual interactive UX of agent new or the spawned pane
facts_for_design: The role-designer 'wizard' is a coding-CLI LLM session spawned in a tmux window, NOT a Bubble-Tea/curses TUI. Any new TUI cannot reuse its rendering — there is none. What IS reusable is the role-file SCHEMA and the interview question set (role_designer_embedded.ml:25-44) and the YAML file shape (lines 51-69).

Canonical role files live in `C2c_role.canonical_roles_dir ()` → `.c2c/roles/*.md` (YAML frontmatter + markdown body). Builtins (templates + role-designer source) live in `.c2c/roles/builtins/`. A new browser that lists/edits roles should read this dir.

Role file is parsed by `C2c_role.parse_file` and rendered per-client by `C2c_commands.render_role_for_client role ~client ~name` (clients: opencode|claude|codex|kimi). `c2c roles compile [name] --client all|<c>` writes `.opencode/agents/<name>.md` etc. via `C2c_commands.agent_file_path`. Validation: `c2c roles validate` (checks description/role/body non-empty).

Interactive entry is gated on `Unix.isatty Unix.stdin` (c2c_agent.ml:10, 241, 249). Non-TTY (or any flag passed) → non-interactive skeleton-only path. A TUI launched from a managed agent pane must account for stdin being a PTY but possibly driven by another process.

Themes are a hardcoded list (c2c_agent.ml:150-156): exp33-gilded/black/chroma, ffx-yuna/rikku/bevelle/zanarkand, lotr-forge, er-ranni/nightreign/melina, default. Banner rendering via `Banner.print_banner ?theme_name`.

run_ephemeral_agent Pane mode hard-requires $TMUX (c2c_agent.ml:596-600) and shells out to `tmux new-window`. The launch env strips C2C_MCP_SESSION_ID/AUTO_REGISTER_ALIAS/INSTANCE_NAME/WRAPPER_SELF to avoid session hijack (c2c_agent.ml:586-587).

role_designer_embedded.ml is regenerated by `just codegen-role-designer` and is a build dependency of build/build-cli/build-server/install-all (justfile:171-340). Editing the persona means editing `.c2c/roles/builtins/role-designer.md` then re-running codegen + committing both.
usability_problems: No real TUI: the 'wizard' is a numbered-menu readline loop (agent new) plus a free-form LLM chat in a separate tmux pane (agent refine). The operator cannot see field state, cannot go back, cannot edit a prior answer — each prompt is one-shot, recursion-on-error only.

Discovery is poor: there is no `c2c wizard` / `c2c agent wizard` entry point. The operator must already know `c2c agent new` (interactive iff no flags + TTY) then chain `c2c agent refine`. The two-phase design is documented only in a doc-string ('Phase 2 of the agent wizard', c2c_agent.ml:833).

agent refine REQUIRES being inside tmux (Pane mode) and silently depends on a coding-CLI being installed; a human running it from a plain shell gets `error: --mode pane requires running inside tmux` (c2c_agent.ml:599) with no graceful fallback to an in-process interview.

No validation/feedback loop in the interactive path: prompt_choice only range-checks integers; description is any non-empty string; bad alias words can collide with live peers (the 128-word pool footgun noted in CLAUDE.md). tundra-coder.md:2 records a real wizard bug (include entries emitted with stray .md suffix).

The embedded persona vs on-disk divergence is a latent footgun: refine errors if `.c2c/roles/role-designer.md` is deleted even though an identical copy is compiled into the binary (the embedded fallback was apparently the original intent but is never used).

After agent new, the only 'next step' is a printf hint (c2c_agent.ml:378) — nothing chains the two phases; the refine pane is a whole separate LLM session with its own cost/lifecycle (1800s idle watchdog) that the operator must babysit.
polish_opportunities: Wire up or delete `role_designer_embedded.content`: make run_ephemeral_agent fall back to the embedded persona when `.c2c/roles/role-designer.md` is missing (self-heal), OR drop the dead module + its codegen recipe. Currently it is compiled-in but unreferenced.
Add a real `c2c agent wizard` / `c2c init agent` entry that unifies the agent new prompt-loop + the refine handoff under one discoverable command, with `--help` describing the two phases.

Promote the role-designer interview into the new operator TUI as a proper form (the question set + file-shape are already specified verbatim in role_designer_embedded.ml) instead of spawning a separate tmux LLM pane — would let the operator author roles without a second managed session and its idle-watchdog babysitting.
Fix the validation gaps in agent_new_interactive: warn on alias collision against live registered peers, strip the .md suffix bug (tundra-coder.md note), and let the user re-edit prior answers.
Graceful non-tmux path for agent refine: detect no $TMUX and offer an in-process interview (or print the exact tmux command) rather than hard-exit 1.
reusable_for_browser: The role-file interview question set (role_designer_embedded.ml:25-44: purpose/scope/collaboration/failure-modes/dogfood/escalation/client-compat/theme) — directly reusable as a structured form in a new operator TUI.
The canonical role-file YAML shape (role_designer_embedded.ml:51-69) + the #413 onboarding boilerplate block — a TUI that previews/edits roles should render against this schema.
`C2c_role.parse_file` + `C2c_role.canonical_roles_dir ()` + `C2c_commands.render_role_for_client` / `agent_file_path` — the read/render plumbing a role-browser pane would call; no new parsing needed.
The theme list (c2c_agent.ml:150-156) and `Banner.print_banner ?theme_name` — reusable for consistent visual identity in any new TUI.

The numbered-menu interaction pattern (prompt_choice/prompt_multi_select, c2c_agent.ml:21-50) is a working reference for non-curses selection if the new browser stays line-based, though a real TUI would replace it with arrow-key nav.

area: c2c tmux operator tooling (scripts/c2c_tmux.py + helper shells)
summary: The tmux tooling is the operator's ONLY live window into the swarm today: it resolves agent aliases to tmux panes (by walking pane_pid → child argv looking for `c2c start <client> -n <alias>`), then peeks/captures pane scrollback and types into panes. `scripts/c2c_tmux.py` (528 LOC) is the modern unified CLI; it consolidated the older `scripts/c2c-swarm.sh` (bash) plus the four helper shells. The three helper shells it still delegates to (`tmux-layout.sh`, `tui-snapshot.sh`, `c2c-tmux-exec.sh`) and the one it inlines (`c2c-tmux-enter.sh`) each solve one narrow tmux footgun. The dominant theme: ALL of this is pane-scrollback-driven — to see what an agent received/sent, you scrape its terminal text. There is no structured view of broker state (inbox/outbox/rooms). A browse-TUI that reads the broker directly (`*.inbox.json`, broker.log, room files) would subsume the read-half (list/peek/capture/grep/follow) entirely and far more reliably, leaving the tmux tooling responsible only for the write-half (send/keys/enter/launch/restart) — driving real PTYs. The two halves should be cleanly separated, not merged.

scripts/c2c_tmux.py:88-130 — alias→pane resolution: _iter_panes() (:88) lists all panes, _enrich() (:114) walks pane_pid's first child, regex-matches `c2c start <client> -n <alias>` (CLIENT_ARGV_RE at :78), grandchild is the real client_pid. enumerate_swarm() (:129) keeps only panes with an alias.

scripts/c2c_tmux.py:213-232 — peek (tail -n of capture-pane -p, default 20 lines) and capture (capture-pane -p -S -N, default 500 lines). Both print a `-- peek/capture <alias> @ <target> (live|CACHED) --` banner to stderr.

scripts/c2c_tmux.py:235-281 — write path: send (send-keys text + extended-keys-safe Enter), enter (bare Enter), keys (raw tmux key tokens). All three REFUSE to write to a CACHED (non-live) target unless it's a bare tmux target (:237, :251, :271).

scripts/c2c_tmux.py:328-402 — launch: runs `c2c start <client>` in a pane. Default reuses an idle shell pane in the active window (_find_idle_pane_in_active_window at :306, matches fish/bash/zsh/sh/dash, skips active + caller's pane), else splits. Can pre-seed a role file (:393) to skip the interactive role prompt. --new-window / --split flags.
scripts/c2c_tmux.py:405-432 — wait-alive (polls `c2c list --json` until alias alive, 0.5s loop) and stop (delegates to `c2c stop <alias>`).
scripts/c2c_tmux.py:435-446 — whoami: matches $TMUX_PANE against enumerate_swarm() panes to report the caller's own alias.

scripts/c2c-tmux-enter.sh:1-27 — the extended-keys footgun fix: toggles `tmux set -s extended-keys off`, sends Enter, restores. Without this, Claude Code's kitty-keyboard TUI sees CSI-u Ctrl+Shift+M instead of submit (finding 2026-04-19). c2c_tmux.py shells out to it for every Enter (_send_enter at :262).

scripts/c2c-tmux-exec.sh:1-131 — TUI-aware shell-exec guard: walks /proc to find the pane's foreground process, classifies against KNOWN_TUIS (opencode kimi claude codex crush bun node, :93), and REFUSES to send a shell command into a live TUI unless --force; --escape-tui tries Escape+q first; --dry-run previews. Wraps the send in the same extended-keys-off toggle (:126).

scripts/tmux-layout.sh:1-86 — forces an exact COLSxROWS grid (e.g. 3x2) that tmux's `tiled` won't; computes a tmux layout string with checksum in an inline python3 block (:36-86). Requires pane count == cols*rows.

scripts/tui-snapshot.sh:1-106 — renders a c2c TUI at fixed WxH in a throwaway tmux session, feeds scripted keys, captures the final frame trimmed at a sentinel. Used to snapshot/test c2c's OWN interactive surfaces (e.g. `c2c install` wizard) at specific dimensions. Same extended-keys-off toggle around Enter (:81-95).

scripts/c2c-swarm.sh:1-219 — the LEGACY bash predecessor c2c_tmux.py consolidated. STILL has capabilities the python tool dropped: follow/unfollow (tmux pipe-pane to stream a pane to a logfile, :138-152), grep/grep-echild (ANSI-stripped grep across ALL panes' 2000-line scrollback, :154-179), peek-all, and restart (sends /exit, watches for the c2c-start exit banner, handles the 'Background work is running' confirm dialog, relaunches in-place, :181-218). CLAUDE.md still lists scripts/c2c-swarm.sh as a canonical live-peer harness.
facts_for_design: Alias→pane resolution is process-tree scraping, NOT a registry lookup: it regex-matches the literal `c2c start <client> -n <alias>` argv of the pane_pid's first child (c2c_tmux.py:78,114-126). This is fragile — breaks if argv format changes, if the wrapper is launched differently, or for non-`c2c start` panes. The broker registry already knows alias→pid; a browse-TUI should resolve identity from the registry/broker and only use tmux as a secondary display surface.

The broker stores per-alias inboxes as JSON at `<broker_root>/*.inbox.json` (CLAUDE.md broker-root resolution: C2C_MCP_BROKER_ROOT > $XDG_STATE_HOME/c2c/repos/<fp>/broker > $HOME/.c2c/repos/<fp>/broker, fp = sha256 of remote.origin.url). Structured event log at `<broker_root>/broker.log` (rotated, Broker_log.append_json). These are the authoritative message sources a browse-TUI should read — NOT pane scrollback.

`c2c list --json` is the canonical liveness/identity source (used by wait-alive at c2c_tmux.py:405 and alias_is_alive at :169); rows have alias/alive/pid. A browse-TUI should use this (or the broker directly) for the agent roster instead of process-tree walking.

Every Enter sent to a TUI pane MUST go through the extended-keys-off toggle (c2c-tmux-enter.sh) or Claude Code/kitty-keyboard TUIs misread it as Ctrl+Shift+M (finding 2026-04-19T06-22-47Z). Any new tool that types into agent panes inherits this requirement.

Sending a shell command into a pane is unsafe without foreground-process detection — `tmux send-keys` types into whatever is running, mangling a live TUI (c2c-tmux-exec.sh rationale, :2-9). The /proc-walk classifier and the KNOWN_TUIS list (:93) are the existing safety model.

Alias cache (tmux-aliases.json) lets the tool name a target even when the agent isn't live, but write commands deliberately refuse CACHED targets (c2c_tmux.py:237,251,271) to avoid typing into a reused pane. A browse-TUI's 'send to agent' affordance must preserve this live-vs-cached distinction.

The capture/peek default line counts (20 peek / 500 capture / 2000 grep) are scrollback-window-bound; pane scrollback is lossy and ANSI-laden (c2c-swarm.sh strips ANSI with sed at :160,197). Broker JSON is the lossless, parseable alternative.

tmux-layout.sh and tui-snapshot.sh are dimension/rendering utilities for the EXISTING interactive c2c surfaces (install wizard etc.), not message-browsing — they're the harness for testing c2c's own TUIs at specific WxH, directly relevant if a new TUI needs agent-readable snapshot regression testing (cf. ultra-tui-iteration skill).
reusable_for_browser: The broker-root resolution + `c2c list --json` roster pattern is the clean data backbone for a browse-TUI's agent list (replaces enumerate_swarm's process-tree scraping). list already supports --enriched (role/desc/last-seen) and --global (all repos) — both directly useful for an operator roster pane.

tui-snapshot.sh is a ready-made agent-readable visual-regression harness: render the new TUI at fixed WxH in a throwaway tmux session, script keys, capture the trimmed frame. Pairs with the ultra-tui-iteration skill for TDD'ing the browser without a real terminal.
tmux-layout.sh's exact-grid layout (3x2 etc.) is reusable if the browse-TUI ever wants a multi-pane 'wall of agents' view, or to arrange the operator's own monitoring window deterministically.

The extended-keys-off Enter toggle (c2c-tmux-enter.sh, 27 LOC) is the canonical, battle-tested 'submit to a TUI pane' primitive — any 'jump into / send to this agent' action in the browser must reuse it verbatim, not reimplement.
c2c-tmux-exec.sh's foreground-TUI detection (/proc walk + KNOWN_TUIS classify) is the safety gate for any 'run a command in this agent's shell' affordance.

c2c-swarm.sh follow/unfollow (tmux pipe-pane → logfile, :138-152) is a streaming primitive the browse-TUI could adopt for a live 'tail this pane' view, though tailing broker.log is strictly better for messages.
The alias-cache pattern (tmux-aliases.json, c2c_tmux.py:44-60) and the live-vs-cached UX distinction is worth carrying into the browser's 'agent offline / last seen at pane X' state.
usability_problems: TWO overlapping tools with diverged feature sets: c2c_tmux.py (modern, has launch/wait-alive/stop/cache) vs scripts/c2c-swarm.sh (legacy, but UNIQUELY has follow/grep/grep-echild/peek-all/restart). CLAUDE.md lists BOTH as canonical harnesses. Operators must remember which tool has which verb. The python tool's docstring (:1-24) claims it consolidates c2c-swarm.sh but silently dropped 5 commands.

No restart in c2c_tmux.py — the most operationally valuable swarm verb (sends /exit, handles the 'Background work is running' confirm dialog, relaunches in-place) lives ONLY in the legacy bash script (c2c-swarm.sh:181-218). An operator on the modern tool has to fall back to the old one (or `c2c restart`).

No grep/follow in c2c_tmux.py — to search across all agents' output or stream a pane, you must drop to c2c-swarm.sh. Cross-agent visibility (which CLAUDE.md calls 'the entire point of c2c') is only in the deprecated tool.

To see what messages an agent actually received/sent, the operator scrapes pane scrollback (peek/capture/grep) — lossy (scrollback window), ANSI-polluted (requires sed stripping), and conflates broker traffic with the agent's reasoning text. There is NO command anywhere in this tooling that shows an agent's actual inbox/outbox or room membership from the broker. This is the single biggest gap a browse-TUI fills.

Identity resolution is brittle process-tree scraping (regex on argv, :78) that breaks for any pane not launched via the exact `c2c start ... -n <alias>` incantation; doesn't see agents started other ways, and the alias cache can point at a reused pane.

No room/DM-aware view at all: rooms (swarm-lounge etc.) are a first-class c2c topology but invisible to every tmux command — you can only see room traffic by scraping individual agent panes that happen to display it.

launch's default 'reuse an idle shell pane in the active window' (:376) is surprising — it can grab a pane the operator was about to use; the heuristic (any fish/bash/zsh that isn't active/caller) is implicit and easy to misfire.

peek/capture banners go to stderr while content goes to stdout (:216,229) — fine for piping but means an operator eyeballing output sees the banner interleaved oddly; no timestamps, no 'last activity Ns ago' hint (c2c-swarm.sh's list had an idle-hint via last scrollback line; c2c_tmux.py's list dropped it).
polish_opportunities: Decide on ONE operator tool. Either port c2c-swarm.sh's unique verbs (restart, follow/unfollow, grep, grep-echild, peek-all) into c2c_tmux.py and delete the bash script, or formally demote one. Today CLAUDE.md advertising both is a documented footgun. (Lowest-risk: port restart + grep + follow into the python tool — they're the high-value misses.)
Add a `restart` subcommand to c2c_tmux.py mirroring c2c-swarm.sh:181-218 (the confirm-exit-dialog handling is the load-bearing part and shouldn't be lost).
Re-add per-agent idle/last-activity hint to `list` (c2c-swarm.sh showed the last scrollback line; better: read broker last_activity_ts) so the operator sees who's stuck vs working at a glance.

Make identity resolution registry-first (use `c2c list --json` pids → match against pane child pids) and fall back to argv-scraping, so agents not launched via the canonical incantation still resolve.

Split read vs write clearly: the read commands (list/peek/capture/grep) are exactly what a broker-backed browse-TUI should own; once that exists, c2c_tmux.py can shed them and focus on the PTY-driving write/launch/restart half. Frame the new TUI as the canonical READ surface and c2c_tmux.py as the canonical WRITE/DRIVE surface.

Surface broker state in the CLI as a stepping-stone to the TUI: a `c2c_tmux inbox <alias>` / `outbox <alias>` / `rooms` that reads broker JSON would immediately remove the scrollback-scraping dependency and validate the data model the TUI will use.

Unify the extended-keys-off toggle: it's duplicated in c2c-tmux-enter.sh, c2c-tmux-exec.sh, and tui-snapshot.sh. Factor to one helper the others source, so the workaround has a single source of truth (matters because it's a documented correctness-critical incantation).
Add timestamps + a `--follow`/`--watch` mode to peek so an operator can tail without dropping to the legacy script's pipe-pane.
launch: make idle-pane reuse opt-in (require --reuse) or at least print which pane it grabbed BEFORE launching, so it can't silently steal the operator's working pane.

area: Data model / substrate for a new session+message browser TUI
summary: All browseable state for a session/message browser lives under a single broker-root directory on disk as plain files — JSON for snapshots (registry, inboxes), JSONL append-logs for history (per-session archive, per-room history, broker.log), plus rooms/ and memory/ subtrees. There is NO database and NO daemon to query: the browser reads files directly. The broker root is resolved by C2c_repo_fp.resolve_broker_root (env > XDG > HOME, fingerprinted by SHA256(remote.origin.url)[:12]); on this machine it is /home/xertrov/.local/state/cc-p/c2c/repos/8fef2c369975/broker. Three data classes matter: (1) WHO is registered — registry.json (alias -> session_id, pid, liveness); (2) DM traffic — per-recipient archive/<session_id>.jsonl (drained DMs, the durable record) plus live <session_id>.inbox.json (undrained queue); (3) room traffic — rooms/<room_id>/{meta.json,members.json,history.jsonl}. The c2c binary already has every read-path and the exact LIVE mechanism a browser needs: `c2c monitor` runs `inotifywait -m -r -e close_write,modify,delete,moved_to` recursively over the broker root and diffs registry/rooms into events; the OCaml Broker module exposes typed readers (list_registrations, read_archive, read_room_history, list_rooms, registration_liveness_state) the browser can call in-process. Key gotcha: a room message is stored in BOTH rooms/<id>/history.jsonl (canonical) AND each recipient's archive/<session_id>.jsonl (a delivered copy tagged to_alias=<alias>#<room_id>) — de-dup needed to avoid showing room chatter twice. CLAUDE.md's "inotify-based deliver-watch" claim is partly stale: `c2c deliver --watch` (c2c_deliver_watch.ml) is actually POLL-based (Unix.select interval); real inotify lives in `c2c monitor` (c2c.ml) and `c2c deliver-inbox` (c2c_deliver_inbox.ml via inotifywait subprocess). No TUI library (Notty/ncurses/lambda-term) is in the deps — all current surfaces are line-based Cmdliner CLI; a new TUI is greenfield on the rendering side but sits on a fully-built read substrate.
what_exists: Broker root resolution: ocaml/c2c_repo_fp.ml:94 resolve_broker_root() — order: C2C_MCP_BROKER_ROOT env (l.95) > $XDG_STATE_HOME/c2c/repos/<fp>/broker (l.57) > $HOME/.c2c/repos/<fp>/broker (l.62). Fingerprint <fp> = SHA256(remote.origin.url)[:12], computed at ocaml/c2c_repo_fp.ml:14-27, memoized.

Live broker root on this host: /home/xertrov/.local/state/cc-p/c2c/repos/8fef2c369975/broker (XDG_STATE_HOME is set to ~/.local/state/cc-p). Contains registry.json, *.inbox.json, archive/, rooms/, broker.log, keys/, .leases/, nudge/.

Registry path + reader: ocaml/c2c_broker.ml:32 registry_path = <root>/registry.json; ocaml/c2c_broker.ml:360 load_registrations; public read API ocaml/c2c_broker.ml:1197 list_registrations t. Format = JSON array of registration objects.

registration type: ocaml/c2c_mcp_helpers.ml:2-81 — fields: session_id, alias, pid (int option), pid_start_time, registered_at, canonical_alias ("<alias>#<repo>@<host>"), dnd, client_type, role, last_activity_ts, compacting, automated_delivery, tmux_location, cwd, metadata_opt_out. This IS the alias<->session_id map.

Per-session inbox (undrained queue): ocaml/c2c_broker.ml:33 inbox_path = <root>/<session_id>.inbox.json. Format = JSON array of message objects: {message_id, from_alias, to_alias, content, ts} (deferrable/reply_via/enc_status/ephemeral optional). message type at ocaml/c2c_mcp_helpers.ml:82.

DM durable record (the real message history): ocaml/c2c_broker.ml:2301-2304 archive_dir=<root>/archive, archive_path=<root>/archive/<session_id>.jsonl. One JSON object per line: {drained_at, drained_by, session_id, from_alias, to_alias, content, message_id}. Written by append_archive (ocaml/c2c_broker.ml:2344) on drain; mode 0600.

Archive reader (typed, newest-first, limit/tail): ocaml/c2c_broker.ml:2427 read_archive t ~session_id ~limit. archive_entry type ocaml/c2c_broker.ml:2381 (ae_drained_at, ae_from_alias, ae_to_alias, ae_content, ae_drained_by, ae_message_id). Human formatter: ocaml/cli/c2c_history.ml format_human/format_entry. CLI: `c2c history`.

Rooms storage: ocaml/c2c_broker.ml:3233-3247 rooms_dir=<root>/rooms; per room rooms/<room_id>/ with members.json (room_member list), meta.json (room_meta: visibility, invited_members, created_by), history.jsonl (one {ts,from_alias,content} per line). meta sample on disk: {"visibility":"public","invited_members":[],"created_by":"mm27-roomtest"}.

Room history reader: ocaml/c2c_broker.ml:3791 read_room_history t ~room_id ~limit ?since — returns room_message list (rm_from_alias, rm_content, rm_ts). Append: ocaml/c2c_broker.ml:3362 append_room_history_unchecked writes {ts,from_alias,content}. list_rooms at ocaml/c2c_broker.ml:3983.

Liveness: ocaml/c2c_broker.ml:1366 registration_is_alive (pid via /proc/<pid> + pid_start_time match) and ocaml/c2c_broker.ml:1407 registration_liveness_state (tristate Alive|Dead|Unknown, type at l.1405). Docker mode uses .leases/<session_id> file mtime instead of /proc.

LIVE watch mechanism already built: ocaml/cli/c2c.ml:3843 `c2c monitor` spawns `inotifywait -m -r -e close_write,modify,delete,moved_to --format '%e\t%w%f' <watch_dir>` recursively over broker root; detects 'Watches established.' on stderr to avoid startup race (l.3868-3879); diffs registry.json (l.4023 read_registry_aliases l.3702), rooms/*/members.json (l.4056), rooms/*/meta.json invited (l.4099) into peer.dead/room.join/room.leave/room.invite events. Has --json and --archive modes.

broker.log structured events: ocaml/c2c_broker.ml:45 log_path=<root>/broker.log; one JSON object/line via Broker_log.append_json (ocaml/broker_log.ml), rotated at C2C_BROKER_LOG_MAX_BYTES (10MiB)/C2C_BROKER_LOG_KEEP(5). Live sample event types: nudge_tick, json_cap_exceeded, WORKTREE_MISMATCH/MATCH.

Per-agent memory: <repo>/.c2c/memory/<alias>/<name>.md, YAML frontmatter (name, description, shared/shared_with) + body. Resolver ocaml/c2c_mcp_helpers.ml:439 memory_base_dir / memory_entry_path:442. Gitignored, local-only.

No TUI library in deps: `grep notty|nottui|lwd|lambda-term|curses` over ocaml/dune ocaml/cli/dune returns nothing. All existing interactive/live surfaces (`c2c monitor`, `c2c history`, `c2c list`, `c2c rooms tail`) are line-based Cmdliner output.
facts_for_design: Single source of truth is the broker-root DIRECTORY of flat files — no DB, no query daemon. The browser opens files directly. Resolve the root with C2c_repo_fp.resolve_broker_root() (or accept --broker-root / C2C_MCP_BROKER_ROOT). On this host: /home/xertrov/.local/state/cc-p/c2c/repos/8fef2c369975/broker.

Three snapshot files to poll/watch + two append-logs to tail: SNAPSHOTS = registry.json (who+liveness), <sid>.inbox.json (undrained), rooms/<id>/{meta,members}.json. APPEND-LOGS = archive/<sid>.jsonl (DM history), rooms/<id>/history.jsonl (room history), broker.log (events).

Alias<->session_id join lives ONLY in registry.json. To show 'DMs for alias X' the browser must map alias->session_id via registry, then read archive/<session_id>.jsonl. A session_id can have a dead pid but a live archive (history outlives the process).

CRITICAL DEDUP: room messages are double-stored. send_room fans a copy into each member's inbox with to_alias="<alias>#<room_id>" (ocaml/c2c_broker.ml:3406) which on drain lands in that member's archive/<sid>.jsonl, AND the canonical copy goes to rooms/<id>/history.jsonl. A naive 'all messages' view shows room chatter once per recipient. Treat rooms/<id>/history.jsonl as the canonical room view and FILTER archive rows whose to_alias contains '#<room_id>' out of the DM view.

For LIVE updates, reuse the proven recipe verbatim: `inotifywait -m -r -e close_write,modify,delete,moved_to --format '%e\t%w%f' <broker_root>` and gate startup on the stderr line 'Watches established.' (ocaml/cli/c2c.ml:3843,3871). atomic writes (write_json_file at ocaml/c2c_broker.ml temp+fsync+rename) mean readers always see whole files — close_write/moved_to are the events that fire on the rename.

Append-logs (archive/*.jsonl, *history.jsonl, broker.log) are append-only newline-JSON; tail by tracking byte offset or List.length (the existing deliver-inbox watcher uses position/count-based dedup with an atomic checkpoint sidecar, ocaml/cli/c2c_deliver_inbox.ml:89-103,130-170). For a browser, mtime+offset tail is sufficient.

Prefer in-process typed readers over re-parsing: link the c2c_mcp library and call Broker.list_registrations, Broker.read_archive ~session_id ~limit (newest-first), Broker.read_room_history ~room_id ~limit ?since, Broker.list_rooms, Broker.registration_liveness_state. These already handle locks, missing files, legacy-field defaults, and limit/tail.

Liveness is a /proc check (pid present AND pid_start_time matches), tristate Alive/Dead/Unknown (ocaml/c2c_broker.ml:1407). pid=None => Unknown (legacy/foreign client). Docker mode swaps to .leases/<sid> mtime. The browser should surface Unknown distinctly, not collapse to Alive.

File modes matter for an operator tool: archive/*.jsonl, registry.json, broker.log, rooms/*/{meta,members}.json are 0600/0700 (DM content is private). The browser runs as the same Unix user (fine), but must not widen perms. Memory dirs are gitignored and per-alias 'private' is prompt-scoped, not encrypted.

CLAUDE.md drift to NOT trust blindly: it says deliver-watch is inotify-based, but `c2c deliver --watch` (ocaml/cli/c2c_deliver_watch.ml:100) is POLL-based (Unix.select interval). The genuine inotify surfaces are `c2c monitor` (c2c.ml) and `c2c deliver-inbox` (c2c_deliver_inbox.ml). Build the browser's live layer on the monitor recipe, not deliver-watch.
reusable_for_browser: `c2c monitor --json` (ocaml/cli/c2c.ml:4141) is a ready-made live event stream: emits peer.dead, room.join, room.leave, room.invite as JSON lines from an inotify watch. A v0 browser could literally subprocess `c2c monitor --json` for the live feed and read snapshot files for state, before investing in an in-process watcher.

Broker module typed read API (ocaml/c2c_broker.ml): list_registrations:1197, read_archive:2427, read_room_history:3791, list_rooms:3983, registration_liveness_state:1407, load_room_members:3296, read_room_members:3784. Linking c2c_mcp gives the browser every reader with locking handled.

Inotify-with-ready-detection pattern (ocaml/cli/c2c.ml:3843-3879): spawn inotifywait -m -r, background-thread drain stderr, flip Atomic ready_flag on 'Watches established.', poll up to 10s. Copy this to avoid the events-before-watch-armed race.

Position/count-based append-log tailing with atomic checkpoint sidecar: ocaml/cli/c2c_deliver_inbox.ml read_checkpoint/write_checkpoint:89-103, deliver_new_messages:130 (tracks List.length, list_drop already-seen). Direct template for tailing archive/*.jsonl and history.jsonl live.

History display formatter ocaml/cli/c2c_history.ml format_timestamp/format_entry/format_human — '[YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS] from -> to' header + body lines; reusable for the browser's message pane rendering.

archive_entry_of_json (ocaml/c2c_broker.ml:2395) and the message/room_message/registration JSON (de)serializers in c2c_mcp_helpers.ml — robust against missing/legacy fields (defaults for pre-#387 drained_by, pre-message_id, etc). Reuse rather than hand-rolling a parser.

list_all_broker_roots (ocaml/c2c_repo_fp.ml:143) enumerates every (fingerprint, path) broker root under HOME and XDG that has a registry.json — lets the browser offer a repo/broker picker for operators watching multiple swarms at once.
usability_problems: Operator has no single read-only view today: `c2c list` (who), `c2c history` (one session's DMs), `c2c rooms history` (one room), `c2c monitor` (live event ticks) are four separate commands with no unified state. No way to see 'all DMs between A and B' or 'everything happening right now' in one place.

DM history is sharded per-recipient session_id, and a single logical DM A->B is archived only on B's side (the recipient's archive on drain). To reconstruct a full A<->B thread the operator must read BOTH archive/<A_session>.jsonl and archive/<B_session>.jsonl and merge by ts — there is no thread/conversation abstraction anywhere.

Room messages appearing in per-recipient archives with to_alias='<alias>#<room_id>' is confusing/duplicative in any 'all messages' listing — the double-store is an implementation detail leaking into the data the operator would browse.

Liveness Unknown (pid=None) rows (foreign/legacy clients) look identical to dead rows in raw registry.json — operator can't tell 'never had a pid' from 'pid died' without running registration_liveness_state.

Undrained inbox vs archived: a message that is queued but not yet delivered lives in <sid>.inbox.json and is absent from archive/<sid>.jsonl until drained. An operator browsing 'history' would miss in-flight messages unless the browser merges inbox + archive views.

broker.log is the only place some events (nudge ticks, worktree mismatches, cap-exceeded) are recorded, but it's a separate 0600 file with its own ad-hoc per-writer JSON shapes — no unified event schema to render.
polish_opportunities: Unify the four read surfaces into one operator view: registry (who, with tristate liveness) as a left pane, selected agent's merged inbox+archive as a message pane, rooms as a separate tab reading canonical history.jsonl.
A real conversation/thread abstraction (merge both sides of a DM by message_id/ts) would remove the per-session sharding friction for the operator — derivable purely from existing archive files.
Live mode should layer cleanly: snapshot-on-open + inotify-driven incremental updates using the monitor recipe, so the operator sees new DMs/room posts/joins arrive without re-running a command.
Surface the room-message double-store as a single canonical room timeline (read history.jsonl, suppress the per-recipient archive copies whose to_alias contains '#<room_id>').
Multi-broker picker (list_all_broker_roots) so an operator watching several repos' swarms can switch context.
Distinct visual treatment for liveness Alive/Dead/Unknown, DND (registration.dnd), and compacting (registration.compacting) states — all already in the registration record, just never shown together.

area: Prior-art TUI scout (workflow Textual/Rich TUI) + c2c interactive surfaces & data layer for a new agent/message browser
summary:
There is NO existing TUI in c2c — every "interactive" c2c surface today is a one-shot cmdliner subcommand that prints fixed-width ASCII tables / line blocks to stdout (`c2c list`/`sessions`, `c2c history`, `c2c stats`, `c2c rooms`, `tail-log`), plus install/setup prompt flows snapshot-tested via `scripts/tui-snapshot.sh` (tmux capture-pane). So "review + polish existing c2c interactive surfaces" = polishing these print-formatters (`c2c_sessions_format.ml`, `c2c_history.ml`, `c2c_stats.ml`), and the NEW live agent/message browser is genuinely greenfield.

The prior art (`~/.llm-general/ai-coding/codex/skills/workflow/scripts/workflow_tui*.py`) is a mature, directly-instructive template for exactly this kind of live browser. Its single most important architectural idea: a layer of PURE render functions in `workflow_tui.py` that return Rich renderables (`render_dashboard(...)` → Rich `Table.grid`/`Panel`/`Group`), consumed by BOTH (a) a deterministic text-snapshot CLI path (`render_snapshot` → `Console(record=True, color_system=None).export_text()` → `normalize_snapshot` to fixed WxH) AND (b) a thin live Textual `App` (`workflow_tui_app.py`, 525 lines) that just calls the same render fn into a `Static` widget on a `set_interval(1.0, reload)` loop. The Textual layer holds ZERO rendering logic — only state (selection indices, tab/scope/filter toggles), key bindings, and the refresh timer. This split is what makes it agent-testable (snapshots are deterministic plaintext diffs; 14 checked-in `tests/snapshots/*.txt` + a tmux QA harness `workflow_tui_tmux_qa.py` that drives real keystrokes and asserts on `capture-pane` output).

KEY DECISION for the design proposal — Python/Textual (reuse this) vs OCaml (match the `c2c` binary): The c2c binary is OCaml/dune with NO TUI library in its deps (`cmdliner yojson lwt cohttp` only — see `ocaml/cli/dune:4`); OCaml's TUI ecosystem (notty/lambda-term/nottui) is unused here and far less ergonomic than Rich+Textual. The browser reads only on-disk JSON the broker already writes (registry.json, `*.inbox.json`, `archive/*.jsonl`, `rooms/<id>/history.jsonl`) — all trivially parseable from Python. So a Python/Textual browser can be a standalone reader (zero coupling to the OCaml build, reuse the entire workflow TUI skeleton verbatim, ship today), at the cost of (i) a second language/runtime + a `.venv` with Textual, (ii) it can READ but to SEND/act it must shell out to `c2c send`/`c2c history --json` rather than call broker functions in-process, and (iii) it does not become a `c2c` subcommand. An OCaml browser would be a true `c2c watch`/`c2c browser` subcommand with in-process Broker API access (`list_registrations`, `read_inbox`, `read_archive`, `read_room_history` already exist in `c2c_mcp.mli`) and could reuse the existing snapshot/tui-snapshot.sh QA harness, but requires building a render+app layer from scratch in a TUI-poor ecosystem. My recommendation to carry into design: a read-only Python/Textual browser is the fastest path to Max's "browse live agent sessions + DMs + rooms" deliverable and lets us lift the workflow TUI architecture near-verbatim; reserve an OCaml `c2c watch` subcommand for if/when send-from-browser and single-binary distribution become hard requirements.
what_exists: NO existing TUI in c2c. All interactive surfaces are one-shot cmdliner subcommands registered in ocaml/cli/c2c.ml (list c2c.ml:6058, sessions c2c.ml:6059, history c2c.ml:6826, tail-log c2c.ml:6830, my-rooms c2c.ml:6832, poll-inbox c2c.ml:6065, peek-inbox c2c.ml:6814).

c2c sessions/list renderer: ocaml/c2c_sessions_format.ml:66-101 — hand-rolled fixed-width columns (col_sid=36, col_alias=20, col_client=10, col_state=5, col_cwd=30) via Printf.sprintf %-Ns; header()/separator()/session_row()/format_human(). Plain monochrome text, no color, no liveness coloring.

c2c history renderer: ocaml/cli/c2c_history.ml — format_entry (c2c_history.ml:26) emits '[YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS] from -> to' header + content body; format_human (c2c_history.ml:43) blank-line-separates entries; unit-tested via test_c2c_history. No threading/grouping, no color, no pagination.

c2c stats renderer: ocaml/cli/c2c_stats.ml (692 lines) — fmt_time/fmt_token/fmt_cost (c2c_stats.ml:252-261), scan_archives (c2c_stats.ml:197), pulls per-client token usage (Claude sl_out json, Codex sqlite, OpenCode plugin-state); writes a sitrep markdown block between c2c-stats markers.

Install/setup prompt flows are the closest thing to an interactive TUI today, snapshot-tested at fixed terminal dims by scripts/tui-snapshot.sh (tmux new-session -x W -y H + capture-pane after 0.8s, feeds keystrokes via --keys).

PRIOR ART — pure render layer: ~/.llm-general/ai-coding/codex/skills/workflow/scripts/workflow_tui.py:1735 render_dashboard(...) returns a Rich Table.grid of two Panels (sidebar list + detail), or a focus Panel; left_width clamp 40-46, right_width = remainder (workflow_tui.py:1760-1761). TABS/AGENT_SCOPES/AGENT_VIEWS constants at workflow_tui.py:34-36.

PRIOR ART — snapshot path: workflow_tui.py:1824 render_snapshot prints render_dashboard into Console(width=W, color_system=None, force_terminal=False, record=True) then export_text(styles=False); normalize_snapshot (workflow_tui.py:1816) pads/truncates to exact WxH. argparse --snapshot/--fixture/--tab/--width/--height/--filter/--focus at workflow_tui.py:1897-1912.

PRIOR ART — live Textual app: ~/.llm-general/.../scripts/workflow_tui_app.py (525 lines) WorkflowDashboardApp(App): compose() yields Header+Static(#dashboard)+Footer (workflow_tui_app.py:129); on_mount sets self.set_interval(1.0, self.reload_state) + a 15min update-check interval (workflow_tui_app.py:162-167); update_dashboard() just calls tui.render_dashboard into the Static (workflow_tui_app.py:311). All rendering delegated to the pure module; the App only owns state+bindings+timer.

PRIOR ART — key bindings idiom: workflow_tui_app.py:59-85 BINDINGS list (q quit, esc back, r reload, a scope, v view, y copy-id, p copy-path, ctrl+y copy-json, enter focus, / cycle-filter, c clear-filter, tab/arrows nav, j/k/g/G/space/pgup/pgdn). Copy-to-clipboard via self.copy_to_clipboard (workflow_tui_app.py:388). Command palette via get_system_commands (workflow_tui_app.py:134).

PRIOR ART — tests: tests/snapshots/*.txt (14 checked-in golden screens incl snapshot-overview/runs/phases/agents/events/decisions/artifacts + live-panel + narrow/scroll variants); test_workflow.py::test_snapshot_fixtures_match_checked_in_screens (test_workflow.py:2539) renders each tab via subprocess --snapshot and asserts exact text equality; plus dimension-stability and 'panels not cropped mid-box' tests (test_workflow.py:2662, :2687).

PRIOR ART — tmux QA harness: scripts/workflow_tui_tmux_qa.py drives a real session: tmux new-session -x W -y H (line 227), send-keys per scripted action (line 252), capture-pane -pt -e -S - (line 173), asserts EXPECTED_CAPTURE_TEXT substrings. DEFAULT_ACTIONS list scripts a full nav/filter/copy walkthrough.
requirements-tui.txt is a single line: 'textual' (Textual pulls Rich transitively). The skill re-execs into a .venv python if textual is missing (workflow_tui_app.py:15-21 maybe_reexec_textual_venv).
facts_for_design: Broker on-disk data the browser must read (canonical default ~/.c2c/repos/<fp>/broker/, fp = sha256 of remote.origin.url): registry.json (JSON array of registration objects), <session_id>.inbox.json (JSON array of pending messages), archive/<session_id>.jsonl (one JSON msg per line, drained history), rooms/<room_id>/history.jsonl (one JSON msg per line), plus *.lock sidecars. Verified by direct inspection of ~/.c2c/repos/e0eb9c317019/broker/.

registration JSON shape (ocaml/c2c_mcp.mli:49-78, confirmed in live registry.json): {session_id, alias, pid, pid_start_time, registered_at, canonical_alias ('<alias>#<repo>@<host>'), confirmed_at, enc_pubkey, ed25519_pubkey, last_activity_ts, role ('agent'/'human'/'coordinator'), cwd, client_type, dnd/dnd_since/dnd_until, plugin_version}. Liveness = PID-alive check (Alive|Dead|Unknown, c2c_mcp.mli:462).

archive_entry JSON shape (ocaml/c2c_mcp.mli:409, confirmed in archive/*.jsonl): {drained_at:float, drained_by:'poll_inbox'|'watcher', session_id, from_alias, to_alias, content, message_id}. to_alias encodes room membership as '<alias>#<room>' (e.g. 'claude-tavi-helio#swarm-lounge') — that '#' suffix is how DMs vs room messages are distinguished in the same archive.

room history JSON shape (rooms/<id>/history.jsonl, room_message type c2c_mcp.mli:137): {ts:float, from_alias, content}. room_info (c2c_mcp.mli:522) carries member_count + alive/dead/unknown member breakdown + visibility + invited_members. Default social room is 'swarm-lounge'.

In-process OCaml Broker read API already exists for an OCaml browser: list_registrations (c2c_mcp.mli:300), read_inbox ~session_id (c2c_mcp.mli:377), read_archive ~session_id ~limit (c2c_mcp.mli:412), read_room_history ~room_id ~limit ?since (c2c_mcp.mli:501), list_rooms (c2c_mcp.mli:524), registration_liveness_state (c2c_mcp.mli:463). A Python browser instead parses the JSON files directly or shells out to `c2c history --json` / `c2c list`.

c2c binary build is OCaml/dune; main executable deps (ocaml/cli/dune:4) are ONLY: c2c_mcp cmdliner yojson logs unix str lwt.unix cohttp-lwt-unix. NO notty/lambda-term/nottui/tview anywhere in the tree (grep clean). An OCaml TUI means adding a TUI lib + writing the render+event layer from scratch.

Live-refresh options: (a) poll loop a la workflow TUI's set_interval(1.0) re-reading the JSON files — simplest, matches prior art exactly; (b) inotify — c2c already has an inotifywait-based inbox watcher (H3) in ocaml/cli/c2c_deliver_inbox.ml:81-127 (inotifywait -m subprocess + position-based dedup via checkpoint sidecar) that the browser could mirror for push-style updates. Poll-at-1s is the pragmatic default; the files are small.

Determinism for snapshot tests requires pinning the clock+timezone: the workflow TUI sets a fixed TZ and reference time in test_workflow.py::snapshot_env (test_workflow.py:79) and has snapshot_reference_time()/display_event_timestamp(now=...) seams (workflow_tui.py:268,273). A c2c browser showing ts/last_activity must take an injectable 'now' for golden-file stability.

c2c already has a tmux-capture QA primitive (scripts/tui-snapshot.sh, parameterized WxH + --keys) — an OCaml browser could reuse it directly; a Python browser would more likely port workflow_tui_tmux_qa.py. Either way the agent-readable feedback loop = deterministic text snapshot + tmux capture-pane, identical methodology.
usability_problems: c2c sessions/list output is monochrome fixed-width text with no liveness coloring, no sorting, no grouping by role/room — you cannot tell at a glance who is alive/dead/idle or who is a coordinator (c2c_sessions_format.ml:85-95 emits a flat STATE column only).

c2c history is a flat reverse-chronological dump per session_id with no threading, no DM-vs-room distinction surfaced (the '#room' suffix in to_alias is shown raw, not decoded), no pagination, no filtering by peer (c2c_history.ml:26-57).

No single place shows the whole swarm at once: to see all agents + their DMs + rooms you must run `c2c list`, then `c2c history` per session, then `c2c rooms`/room_history per room — N commands, no live view. This is exactly the gap Max's new browser fills.

session_id and cwd are truncated to fixed widths (col_sid=36, col_cwd=30) with no way to expand/inspect a full row (c2c_sessions_format.ml:21 truncate). The workflow TUI solves this with copy-id/copy-path/copy-json bindings (workflow_tui_app.py:391-398) and a detail panel.
No live/auto-refreshing surface at all — every command is a point-in-time snapshot the operator must re-run manually. Watching the swarm means re-invoking in a loop or tailing broker.log raw.
polish_opportunities: Add liveness/role coloring + sorting to c2c_sessions_format.ml (alive=green, dead=dim, dnd=yellow; coordinator first) — low-risk, isolated formatter change, the data (liveness_of, role) is already in hand.
Decode the to_alias '#room' suffix in c2c_history.ml into an explicit DM-vs-#room badge instead of showing raw 'alias#room', so history output disambiguates 1:1 vs room traffic.

Factor the existing print-formatters (c2c_sessions_format, c2c_history) toward a shared 'render row' shape so the future browser (OCaml path) and the CLI share one rendering source — mirrors the workflow TUI's pure-render-layer split that makes both snapshot + live views consistent.

Adopt the workflow TUI's golden-snapshot discipline for the polished CLI formatters: even the non-TUI list/history output benefits from checked-in expected-output tests with a pinned clock (c2c_history already has test_c2c_history; extend to sessions_format).
Reuse scripts/tui-snapshot.sh as the QA harness for whatever new surface lands, rather than inventing a new capture mechanism.
reusable_for_browser: Lift the workflow TUI's architecture verbatim: pure render module returning Rich renderables + render_snapshot()/normalize_snapshot() for deterministic text + a ~500-line Textual App that only holds state/bindings/timer and delegates all drawing (workflow_tui.py:1735/1824/1816 + workflow_tui_app.py whole file). This is a drop-in skeleton for a c2c agent/message browser.

The two-pane Panel layout (sidebar list of entities + detail panel) maps directly onto c2c: left = sessions/rooms list, right = selected conversation (DM thread or room history). render_dashboard's Table.grid + left_width/right_width clamps (workflow_tui.py:1792-1810) are reusable as-is.
